main_body: Open market stall: slate-tiled curved roof on two wooden posts, with a grey stone counter holding a blue water basin at the bottom
top_band: Roof ridge: light grey-blue at rows 1-3, then the tiled slope in mid and dark blue-greys down to row 15. Counter: light grey rim at row 30 with the blue basin interior at rows 31-35
evidence: The roof shows a lighter ridge band above a sloped tile face, with a bright lower edge at rows 14-15 and a dark shadow line at rows 16-17 under the eave, similar to the roofed well reference. The counter has a pale rim around an inset blue basin (rows 31-35), then a grey front face (rows 36-42). Both the roof and the counter show a horizontal surface above a front face. The ridge cap is thin, but the sloped roof surface and the basin carry the top read, so this is not a front elevation with a hat.

style.evidence: The roof is well shaded, with about 5 steps, per-slat highlights and tinted dark navy outlines. The rest is thinner than the reference. The posts are 4px-wide, 25-row orange columns with only a light edge and a dark edge. The grey counter front is a large near-flat block of 2-3 greys with no grain. The basin is a flat blue fill with one highlight bar. Many tiles outside the roof carry only 2-4 colours, so the piece looks flatter than the reference stall and well.
